title: Focus on the Big Picture, Not the Numbers
coreMove: Step back from local metrics and force the whole value pattern into view before deciding what the numbers mean.
sourcePressure: Keep strategy grounded in whole-pattern visual judgment, using the strategy canvas to see strategic sameness and possible divergence instead of drowning in isolated metrics.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the chapter as anti-data or as permission to ignore financial discipline.

sourceAnchors.name: strategy canvas
sourceAnchors.detail: official support defines it as a one-page visual analytic for comparing the current state of play and a possible future value curve
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A single strategy canvas can make scattered numbers behave like one picture, which is the point before the next debate starts.

sourceAnchors.name: O'Reilly expanded-edition contents
sourceAnchors.detail: authorized contents place this chapter early in Part Two, where formulation shifts from concept to visual strategy work
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: This is early formulation work: before the spreadsheet can decide, the team has to see what kind of offer it is building.

hook: Do not open with a competitor scoreboard, a war metaphor, or a generic market map.
Do not use A crowded market is not..., The real strategy is..., or What if growth... as reusable shells.
counterintuition: Avoid Most people assume... but actually... and The opposite is true.
Avoid turning every chapter into competition bad, creativity good.
tryThisNow: Avoid Set a timer for 60 seconds and list... as a repeated action.
Avoid generic reflect on your strategy prompts.
examples: Avoid conference-room whiteboard workshops as the default scene.
Avoid repeating mugs, markers, dosing cups, bike helmets, radiators, bus depots, classrooms, narrow kitchens, or generic dashboard scenes.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: customer support metrics and whole experience mapping
exampleSpecs.audience: a support director whose teams defend separate dashboard wins
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether churn keeps rising despite better local metrics
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she lays refund notes, hold times, and transfer points across the wall and stops another metric defense with the whole pattern
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The tape curls off the painted wall as refund notes reach the doorframe

exampleSpecs.domain: bus route data versus hospital appointment journeys
exampleSpecs.audience: a transit planner under pressure to show data-driven progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether riders reach appointments or only see improved isolated numbers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he realizes route punctuality improved while the hospital journey stayed broken at the transfer point
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Henrik three quarterly reports to notice the 8:10 bus was punctual and still useless

exampleSpecs.domain: catering cost sheets versus office lunch handoff observation
exampleSpecs.audience: an operator choosing which cuts preserve buyer value
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether margin fixes damage the part buyers actually need
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: field observation changes the plan from menu tweaks to labeled team trays when she sees the handoff confusion
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The office pantry fills with identical foil lids and nobody knows which tray belongs to finance

exampleSpecs.domain: after-school strategy maps and parent reaction
exampleSpecs.audience: a school leader redesigning after-school support
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether families trust the new plan and use it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a parent points at the map and reveals the missing value factor: predictable pickup, not more enrichment options
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Where do I stand at 5:45?" the parent asks Matteo, ignoring the robotics column

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital lab specimen flow as one visible path
exampleSpecs.audience: a lab supervisor buried in turnaround reports
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether emergency samples arrive fast enough for treatment decisions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sketches the full specimen path and reveals the handoff nobody owns between elevator and accession desk
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 2:16 p.m., Nina follows a blood tube from trauma bay to the service elevator

exampleSpecs.domain: airport kiosk sales data versus passenger anxiety
exampleSpecs.audience: a concessions manager choosing kiosk placement
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether travelers buy food or abandon the line before boarding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he expects kiosk sales to decide, then field watching reveals the boarding-clock pattern hidden by the data
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What if the lowest-selling kiosk is not bad, just too far from the gate clock?

skillTargets: separate whole-pattern strategy from isolated metric wins
use visual comparison before number debate
detect when local dashboards hide a broken buyer journey

tryThisNowSpec: Put your three favorite metrics aside and sketch the whole buyer path in six boxes before interpreting any one number.
